To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the S4-α complex is formed by an entropically driven, diffusion-controlled process in which the protein binds halide ions to the RNA.
S4 binds the α leader sequence with an apparent Kd of 2 μ m and that the complex formation is driven solely by entropy, i.e. the free energy of binding is negative and equal to -TΔS.

the S4-α leader complex is formed by binding of five S4 molecules to the α mRNA, with a total binding constant of 3 × 10 8 m −6, and that binding is entropy driven by the release of ~ 300 water molecules from the protein and RNA surfaces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the thermodynamics of the interaction between a ribosomal protein, S4, and its cognate mRNA, α.
the thermodynamics of the S4-α complex.
the thermodynamic basis of the repression of α mRNA translation by the binding protein, S4.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
S4 binds to a specific site in α mRNA with a binding constant of 13 m −1, a value that is in excellent agreement with that determined by the in vivo method.
the S4-α complex is formed by the binding of a protein to a nucleic acid in the presence of monovalent and divalent cations.
the S4-α RNA complex is a highly cooperative, salt-dependent, and entropy-driven structure with a core of six to eight base pairs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
S4 binding is driven by a large number of weak interactions with the RNA.
S4 binds α mRNA with a high degree of specificity and that the binding is controlled by a delicate balance of forces.
S4 binding to α mRNA involves a core region with high affinity and a flanking region with low affinity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
S4 binding to α mRNA is a highly cooperative event, which is consistent with the observed repression of translation.
the S4-α complex is a highly cooperative system.
S4 binds α mRNA with a very high affinity.
